stories.title: Hope beneath the waves in Rodrigues

photos.caption: A healthy colony of corals in the lagoons of the South-East coast of Mauritius. It is estimated that coral reefs are home to 25% of marine species, including various fish which depend on coral reefs at some stage of their life cycle. Their preservation is key to safeguarding life underwater.

photos.alt: A crown-of-thorns starfish with long orange-tipped spines feeds on pale branching coral beneath clear blue water.
photos.caption: A crown-of-thorns starfish (COTS) preying on a coral colony. This species of starfish is known for its voracious appetite for coral polyps. Photo : Gérald Rambert 2023

photos.caption: Collecting coral fragments for asexual reproduction requires both knowledge and skill. Participants must be trained to identify suitable healthy coral colonies, carefully collect and handle the fragments, use underwater equipment, and snorkel safely.

photos.caption: In Mauritius, the Adaptation Fund-UNDP Coral Restoration Project involves the active participation of beneficiaries from two NGOs : Eco-Sud and Reef Conservation.

photos.alt: Four women sit on a boat's edge over a white cooler, tying coral fragments to blue lines in clear turquoise water.
photos.caption: Beneficiaries of the Reef Conservation NGO are securing coral fragments obtained from recently collected coral colonies onto ropes. These ropes will later be affixed to tables within coral nurseries where they will grow and later be transplanted to restoration sites. A significant number of women living on the South-East coast of Mauritius have been trained by this NGO to participate in coral restoration activities under the UNDP Coral Reef Restoration Project.

photos.alt: Two women on a boat at sea shape a round wire mesh frame, one smiling at left and the other working at right.
photos.caption: Dominique Veerasamy (right) and Preetima Laverdure (left) are beneficiaries of the Eco-Sud NGO which implements the UNDP Coral Restoration project in Mauritius. They are deploying a wire mesh which are fixed to coral tables on the restoration sites of the NGO.  If conditions are favourable, the will reach the desirable outplanting size.

photos.alt: Snorkelers in wetsuits tend coral fragments laid out on a grid over sandy seabed in clear turquoise water.
Aerial view of turquoise lagoon waters over reef patches, with a small white boat at left and a green coastal village at right under cloudy skies.
photos.caption: The South East Marine Protected Area, found in Rodrigues, is the largest Marine Protected Area of the Republic of Mauritius. It has provided for the island's needs for centuries, and now needs protection to restore its stocks of natural resources.
